name: In-situ low-temperature powder XRD of ammonium nitrate phase transitions from -190 C to 135 C in a TTK 600 chamber
plain_name: Watch a powder's crystal structure change with X-rays while it is cooled to -190 C
description: Powder X-ray diffraction in reflection or transmission geometry in a liquid-nitrogen-cooled non-ambient chamber; five ammonium nitrate phases (Pm-3m, P4bm, Pnma, Pmmm, Pccn) are tracked between 135 C and -40 C and the Pccn phase is followed down to -190 C, which the chamber reaches only under vacuum (1e-2 mbar).
keywords: Watch a powder's crystal structure change with X-rays while it is cooled to -190 C

sources.citation: Anton Paar / PANalytical, TTK 600 - low-temperature chamber, non-ambient attachment for XRD, brochure PN10467 (2009)

requirements.rationale: The phase sequence is recorded from 135 C (408.15 K) down to -190 C (83.15 K).
-190 C is reached only with the sample space evacuated; with gas atmospheres the LN2-cooled stage stops at -150 C.
Optional: the documented low-temperature vacuum condition is 1e-2 mbar.
Optional: the chamber reached -190 C with liquid-nitrogen cooling; another cooling method reaching 83 K would also do.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
